# Terms of use

OpenRadView is free and open source, with no account and nothing to buy. These terms cover this website and how the app is meant to be used. The software license still decides what you may do with the code.

## The software

OpenRadView is licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later. You can use, study, change and share it under that license, including commercially. These terms do not add restrictions to it. The source is at github.com/gyorgysh/openradview. GPL distribution includes the corresponding source or a licence-compliant way to obtain it.

## Intended use [...] ## Intended use

OpenRadView is a viewer for personal education with medical images you own or have permission to use. It has not been clinically validated. Do not use it for diagnosis, screening, monitoring, treatment, emergencies or decisions about care. It does not replace a doctor, a radiologist or other qualified health professional.

Images, orientation, measurements and reconstructions can be incomplete or wrong. Ask a qualified clinician to interpret your scans. If you think you need urgent help, contact local emergency services.

## AI agents [...] ## AI agents

The app has no AI of its own and gives no opinion. You can connect an MCP-capable agent you already use, on your own account. Its replies are experimental AI commentary from that agent and its provider, can be wrong and do not replace professional interpretation. Provider terms apply to data you approve for sharing. An app permission dialog does not itself establish legal compliance or guarantee provider privacy.

## Example scans

The included examples are public research data under their own Creative Commons licenses, credited on the home page. Reuse follows those licenses and the TCIA data usage policy. Do not try to identify or contact the people in them.

results.title: OpenRadView: Free, open-source viewer for your own CT, MRI and X-rays | Product Hunt
results.content:
Point it at the disc, the zip or a folder, and it opens the DICOM or NIfTI files on your computer. You get linked axial, coronal and sagittal views, oblique planes, experimental 3D, and distance and angle measurements. No account, no telemetry, no upload.   
  
It's free, open source, and written in Rust with egui and wgpu, so images render on the GPU: Metal acceleration on Apple Silicon, and it works on Windows and Linux with a dedicated GPU too.

There's no AI inside. If you want, an agent you already use, or a local model, can connect over MCP and ask to see a view. Nothing is shared until you allow it, and the agent's replies can be wrong. [...] It's a personal research project, not certified medical software. If something feels wrong, see a doctor and keep asking questions. Ask a clinician to interpret your scans.  
  
It's an app I hope you never need.
